assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Nitric acid
items.clue: Manufactured from ammonia; used to make ammonium nitrate.

items.label: Ammonium salt
items.clue: Made when the gas from the Haber process reacts with an acid.

items.label: Phosphate rock
items.clue: A mined mineral that must be treated before it can feed crops.

items.label: Single superphosphate
items.clue: Calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate, made using sulfuric acid.

questions.stem: An NPK fertiliser contains compounds of which three elements?

options.text: Nitrogen, phosphorus and krypton, symbol K
Nitrogen, potassium and carbon, from K
Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium salts
Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium

questions.explanation: NPK fertilisers contain compounds of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

questions.stem: Why is an NPK fertiliser described as a formulation?

options.text: Because it is one single compound whose formula contains all three elements
Because it uses only insoluble salts so the rain cannot wash it away
Because it is a mixture of salts blended to give set percentages of N, P and K
Because it is made in one reactor from a single mined raw material

questions.explanation: NPK fertilisers are formulations of various salts containing appropriate percentages of the elements.

questions.stem: Ammonia from the Haber process can be used to manufacture which substances?

options.text: Ammonium salts and nitric acid
Ammonium salts and sulfuric acid
Nitric acid and sulfuric acid
Nitric acid and a compound called NPK

questions.explanation: The specification states that ammonia can be used to manufacture ammonium salts and nitric acid.

questions.stem: Which of these fertiliser raw materials are obtained by mining?

options.text: Phosphate rock and ammonium nitrate, but not the potassium salts
Nitric acid and phosphate rock, but not the potassium salts
Only phosphate rock, since the potassium salts are made in plants
Potassium chloride, potassium sulfate and phosphate rock

questions.explanation: The specification lists these three as obtained by mining.

questions.stem: Why can phosphate rock not be used directly as a fertiliser?

options.text: Because the rock must be dried out before it is spread
Because the phosphate compounds in it do not dissolve
Because the rock must first be ground into a much finer powder
Because it dissolves so readily that the rain washes it away

questions.explanation: Plant roots take up dissolved ions, so the insoluble phosphate must first be made into soluble salts.

questions.stem: Phosphate rock is treated with sulfuric acid. What is produced?

options.text: Calcium sulfate only, with the phosphate left in the rock
Calcium phosphate only, known as triple superphosphate
Ammonium sulfate, which supplies nitrogen and sulfur
Single superphosphate: calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate

questions.explanation: Treating phosphate rock with sulfuric acid gives single superphosphate, a mixture of the two salts.

questions.stem: Phosphate rock is treated with nitric acid. Which products are formed?

options.text: Ammonium nitrate and calcium oxide
Phosphoric acid and calcium nitrate
Calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate
Calcium nitrate and calcium oxide

questions.explanation: Treating phosphate rock with nitric acid produces phosphoric acid and calcium nitrate.

questions.stem: Which salt is produced when phosphate rock is treated with phosphoric acid?

options.text: Calcium phosphate, called triple superphosphate
Calcium sulfate, the salt in single superphosphate
Calcium phosphate mixed with some calcium sulfate
Ammonium phosphate, made from the rock alone

questions.explanation: Phosphoric acid converts phosphate rock into calcium phosphate, known as triple superphosphate.

questions.stem: A student makes ammonium sulfate in the laboratory by titration and crystallisation. How does industrial production of the same salt differ?

options.text: It reacts the ammonia with an alkali rather than an acid
It is carried out in exactly the same way, but with larger apparatus
It runs continuously on a large scale, with reactants recycled
It adds phosphorus and potassium to make the compound NPK

questions.explanation: Industrial production is continuous, large scale and integrated, whereas the laboratory prepares a single small batch.
